answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to weave a cryptographic thread of non-transferable compute bonds before accepting contracts. When a newcomer joins, established peers act as a watchful raven cohort that audits its initial task proofs under a willow Merkle tree, slashing the locked bond if duplicate hardware or timing signatures appear. Because each fake agent demands dedicated compute and forfeits its collateral upon detection, an attacker faces linear hardware costs and negative expected utility.
